svg.text: Proposed JEPA implementation — GlucoseDAO context
our own encoder + our own SSL objective, trained on our own unlabelled glucose · rung 3 of the guide's ladder
Guide's ladder: rung 1 — glucodensity images → small CNN (cheapest, no pretraining) · rung 2 — released pretrained encoder, frozen, embeddings into our model
rung 3 — pretrain the encoder ourselves (this diagram)
The guide calls rung 3 out of scope for a 1.5-week timeline. It is drawn because it is what "our own implementation" means — but rungs 1 and 2 are the cheap checks that should gate it.
Outputs
→ SugarOne integration (see jepa_sugarone_integration_proposed.svg)
three injection points: concat at the bottleneck · FiLM · 4th cross-attention stream

one embedding per patch — for the cross-attention route
project 96 → 32 to use as K / V
mean-pool → z : (B, 96)
one vector per window — for concat / FiLM
reduce to 8 / 16 / 32 (PCA or learned) + rescale
96 raw dims would swamp a 32-wide model — reduce first
encoder.pt — trained JepaEncoder weights (E_θ), plain state_dict

Self-supervised pretraining loop — masked latent prediction (this is what makes it JEPA)
the loss lives in representation space; the model never reconstructs glucose values, so it has no output head and cannot forecast on its own
loss = smooth-L1 ( P(context) , stopgrad( E_ξ(target) ) )

gradients flow only into E_θ and P

Context encoder E_θ — JepaEncoder (trainable)
patch embed + 3 pre-norm blocks, embed_dim 96, 6 heads

Target encoder E_ξ — EMA copy, requires_grad = False
same architecture, no gradients, .eval()
sees only the target patches → (B, N_tgt, 96)
EMA: ξ ← m·ξ + (1−m)·θ
context patches

Multi-block masking (I-JEPA style, scaled down)
sample M = 4 target blocks of 2–4 contiguous patches; context = the remaining patches, target positions removed
16 patches is a much shorter sequence than an image's 196 — block count / size need a sanity pass, not the paper's constants
(B, 16, 96) patch embeddings
View A — raw glucose patches (chosen)
patchify (B, 128) → (B, 16, 8); Conv1d(1 → 96, k = 8, stride 8)
patch = 8 steps = 40 min; instance z-score per window
View B — glucodensity image (rung 1, not wired here)
smooth → 1st / 2nd derivative → three 2-D histograms
(B, 3, 32, 32) → 8×8 spatial patches → a CNN, per the guide
Adapter (our code) — reuse JEPA's math, not its I / O
cut sliding windows: never cross a data gap, never mix two patients in one window → glucose window (B, 128)
train split only — val / test rows must never reach the SSL stage, or every downstream forecasting number is contaminated
Standard table — glucose_data_processing, StandardFieldNames
Loop dataset (public, insulin + carbs, ~1000 participants) · uv sync / uv add — never uv pip install
open decision: the guide says day = 288; we use 128 to match SugarOne
